He is a very nice Prof, he does not mind if you ask a very stupid question or ask the same question again and again, he will try to use another way or example to explain
Although the exam is very easy the theory behind every topic is very difficult, he will explain those theories and proof in class, as the related example question and application.
He knows that most of the students taking this course are engineering students, so he won't ask any questions about the theory or proof in the exam.
About the lecture notes, the notes he gives you are around 150-170 pages. But during the class, he will use the whiteboard very frequently, and make notes on it. But I personly suggest that you just copy the note on the whiteboard, and make a few more remarks beside about what he says is more efficient, since that point he writes on the board is basically is same as the note that he gives you but more concise.

sections.content:
The 1st part of the course was about linear algebra, including matrices, and some special techniques like Gram-Schmidt Process. In my opinion, you had better understand the principle thoroughly such that you do not need to remember the ways of computation, or so-called formulae, given that you have some basic knowledge of matrix computations (M2).

The 2nd part of the course was about differential equation. Only linear differential equations were taught in this course. This part may requires much memorization of techniques for computing, and there were different conditions corresponding to different computation "tricks", like finding the general solutions for linear inhomogeneous equations.

The midterm paper and final paper just contained the 1st and 2nd part RESPECTIVELY, ie no questions about the 1st part were in the final exam. Questions in exams were promised to be similar to the tutorial worksheets. In addition, n the final exam, there was an ODE application question (about terminal velocity). This application question was  chosen from the tutorial worksheet about the ODE application as guaranteed. Some may think that as calculators are not allowed n exam, we can just skip those questions requiring calculators in the worksheets.
